hypothesis: AI hypothesis from stress test 11 (topics/0.23/Doc/STRESS_11_READABLE_FRACTION.md), built on the author's layer 3 (what persists is what manages resources well) and reversed Landauer rule: selection for persistence raises the readable fraction r of the bits a system writes with its energy. For cells, r = (genome bits copied per division) / (energy spent per division / (kT ln 2)). Selection acts more efficiently in species with larger effective population size Ne, so r must rise with Ne once cell size is held fixed.

observable.quantity: partial slope b_Ne in log10 r = a + b_V log10 V + b_Ne log10 Ne across species present in both sources
observable.domain: species with both a growth cost C_G and cell volume V in Lynch and Marinov (2015, PNAS 112, 15690) and an effective population size Ne in Sung et al. (2012, PNAS 109, 18488, PMC3494944); genome size from the same tables where given

prediction_method.description: r per species = 2 x genome size (bp) / (C_G x 50 kJ/mol / N_A / (k T ln 2)) at T = 303 K for every species (growth temperatures not used, AI choice). Ordinary least squares of log10 r on log10 V and log10 Ne; 95 percent t-interval of b_Ne. Species are matched by binomial name; a species missing from either table is dropped and listed. Reported, not deciding: the simple slope of log10 r on log10 Ne without V, and the same fit with Lynch and Marinov's total cost (growth plus maintenance) if both are tabulated.

fixed_parameters: energy per ATP 50 kJ/mol and T = 303 K for all species (both cancel in the slope b_Ne)
cell volume V as tabulated by Lynch and Marinov; no other covariate
if fewer than 8 species are in both tables the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE
no phylogenetic correction (AI choice; stated as a limitation, as in T023)
pass_criterion: PASS if the 95 percent interval of b_Ne lies wholly above 0.
fail_criterion: FAILED if the 95 percent interval of b_Ne lies wholly at or below 0. INCONCLUSIVE otherwise, or under the 8-species rule.
note: Disclosure: the drafter has read Lynch and Marinov's scaling summaries (growth cost about 27 V^0.97 and maintenance about 0.39 V^0.88, in 10^9 ATP) but not their species table; Sung et al.'s Ne values have not been opened. Confounds stated before the run: Ne falls with cell size across life, and cost rises almost in proportion to V, so the simple slope of r on Ne is expected to be positive whatever selection does; the deciding quantity is therefore the partial slope with V held fixed. Small samples are likely (the overlap of the two tables may be under 15 species). Nearest theory: Lynch's drift-barrier hypothesis, which already predicts that larger Ne lets selection trim costs; a PASS would show UET's layer 3 is consistent with it, not a UET-distinct result. A UET-distinct version would need a predicted size for b_Ne, which no current equation gives. All criteria are AI choices for the author to accept or change before approval. Approved by the author in chat on 2026-11-20 as drafted ("Approve and run"); this approval is committed before the Ne table is opened.
